Joe Rogan turns to what first drew Robert Bigelow to UFOs in a segment from his show. Bigelow is the aerospace rich man who funded UFO hunts and built space gear. His love for the topic has shaped the field for years.

Rogan works through the tales told of Bigelow's start: a family sighting, a bought ranch of high strangeness, and deals with the state. He asks why a hard-nosed builder would pour cash into ghosts and craft. The segment is short and rich with lore. Listeners get a quick life sketch of a key funder. The library holds the file as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-ORB4j8Z1W1A:
Rogan watches the Pfizer chief's 2019 comments about pills with sensors in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. The clip shows the CEO describing, with pride, a pill that can signal when a patient has swallowed it. Rogan's reaction is the episode.

He turns the remarks over slowly, asking who such tracking serves and where consent fits in. The talk widens into drug firms, digital monitoring, and the thin line between care and control. The segment is a small artifact of pandemic-era distrust, built around a few sentences of corporate candor that landed very differently than intended.

Section 1901a of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with the Capitol Police Board. It sits in Chapter 29, on the Capitol Police, in a general part of the chapter. The end of the Board is set out first. The Board is to watch over and to back the Capitol Police in its work. It is also to push joint work between the Capitol Police and the two Sergeants at Arms, in their work as keepers of the law, and with Congress.

In line with that end, the Board is to set the wide aims and marks of its main work. Those aims are to raise the skill and the worth of what the Board does. A second clause deals with the make-up of the Board. The text shown is cut off at the head of that clause.

Section 661a of Title 2 of the United States Code sets out definitions for its subchapter on credit reform. It sits in Chapter 17A of that title, on congressional budget matters. The first term defined is direct loan. A direct loan is a payment of funds by the government to a borrower outside the federal sphere. The payment is made under a contract that calls for the funds to be paid back, with or without interest.

The term is stated to take in more than that core case. It covers the purchase of, or a share in, a loan made by another lender. It also covers finance deals that put off payment for more than ninety days. The sale of a government asset on credit is named as a case of that kind. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
